wand.title: Feather wand
wand.intro: Drag the feather around the screen. Pull it away from your kitty, like a little mouse running off — that's what she loves to chase.
wand.tip: Don't wave it right in front of her face. When she pounces, pull the feather away quickly!
wand.stalking: Your kitty is watching the feather …
wand.caught: Got it! Your kitty caught the feather.
wand.feedbackToward: Pull it away from her, not towards her face.
wand.pullAwayA11y: Pull the feather away from your kitty
wand.stageA11y: Play area: your kitty and a feather on a wand. Drag the feather away from her.

result.success: Your kitty played and caught the feather. This game counts for today.

reasons.too_few_moves: The feather needs to run away more often — pull it away many times during the minute.
reasons.not_spread: Keep the feather moving the whole minute, not just for a part of it.
reasons.wrong_technique: Pull the feather away from your kitty, like a mouse running off — not into her face.
reasons.missed_pounces: When your kitty pounces, pull the feather away quickly.
reasons.too_uniform: Move the feather your own way — little stops and starts make the game fun.

scoop.title: Clean the litter
scoop.intro: Your kitty used her litter box. Scoop out every clump so it stays clean for her.
scoop.nothing: The litter box is clean — there's nothing to scoop right now.
scoop.messNearby: There's also a mess next to the box. Clean that up with the clean button.
scoop.success: Great job! The litter box is clean.
scoop.unchanged: The litter box was already clean.

grooming.title: Brush your kitty
grooming.intro: Brush her long fur gently with your finger, stroke after stroke, from head to tail.
grooming.matted: Her fur has a knot. This brushing takes a bit longer ({{seconds}} s) and gets the knot out.
grooming.weekDone: All of this week's brushing is done ✓
grooming.stageA11y: Your kitty. Stroke her with your finger to brush her fur.

result.success: Your kitty's fur is brushed. This brushing counts for the week.

litter_change.title: Change all the litter
litter_change.intro: Once a week all the litter goes out: empty the box, wash it and fill it with fresh litter. Scrub with your finger.
litter_change.weekDone: This week's litter change is done ✓
litter_change.weekOpen: Change the litter {{when}} at the latest.
litter_change.overdue: Last week's change was missed, so the box smells — scoop quickly until you change it.
litter_change.stageA11y: The litter box. Scrub it with your finger.

result.success: All the litter is fresh. This week's change is done.

reasons.too_few_strokes: A few more strokes next time — keep going until the time is up.
reasons.not_spread: Keep going through all three steps, right to the end.
reasons.too_uniform: Stroke your own way — a little faster, a little slower.

scratching.title: To the scratching post
scratching.intro: Your kitty scratched the sofa. She isn't naughty — cats need to scratch. Carry her to her scratching post and praise her right away when she scratches it.
scratching.never: Never shout or punish — just show her the right place and praise her.
scratching.nothing: Your kitty hasn't scratched anything. All good!
scratching.dueAt: Show her the scratching post {{when}} at the latest.
scratching.start: Carry her to the scratching post
scratching.carrying: You're carrying her to the scratching post …
scratching.landed: She's scratching the post — praise her now!
scratching.waitHint: A little early — this time it won't count, try again.

result.success: She loves her scratching post. The sofa is safe now.

reasons.too_early: A little early — praise her when she's scratching the post.
reasons.too_late: A little late — praise her right when she scratches the post.
reasons.no_praise: She scratched the post — praise her next time!

firstAid.title: Good to know
firstAid.body: A real cat must never go without food for long. If a cat stops eating, she needs to see a vet soon.

contract.bodyMaineCoon:
I promise to take good care of my virtual kitty, every single day:

• I will feed her at the right time.
• I will give her fresh water every day.
• I will clean her litter box every day and change all the litter once a week.
• I will play with her every day so she stays healthy and happy.
• I will brush her regularly so her fur doesn't get knotted.
• I will act on warnings before she gets sick or has to go to the virtual shelter.

Do you accept this responsibility?

firstAid.title: Good to know
firstAid.body: For a real cat, not eating is serious: a cat that stops eating can develop a dangerous liver disease (hepatic lipidosis). If a cat stops eating, contact a vet promptly — don't wait.
